Prior review retained below:
Re-read all 240 response rationales against their individual question wording, agreement directions and cited institutional scope in a distinct pass. Verified Kristersson caretaker status after 17 September 2026; future coalition pledges and the 2027 benefit cap are not enacted-policy evidence. Reviewed June 2026 firearms changes, July asylum changes and October family rules, distinguishing current entitlements and transitional rules. Corrected the tariffs source date field. Rechecked public-service foundation ownership, non-confessional schooling versus ceremonial religion, minimum wages versus collective bargaining, and local taxes versus national equalisation. Trait-specific health guidance supports mixed causation where it expressly combines biological development and social experience. Kept Culture/Nature Q2 national IQ, Q5 general interests and Q10 immediate moral reactions unknown rather than treating related programmes as comparative causal evidence. Military Q4 was changed from a weak disagreement inference to unknown after finding an inquiry manual allowing imminent-attack defence without establishing its current adoption. Strengthened arms-control and enhancement citations; brain-implant answers remain qualified regulatory/ethics inferences, not claims of an implant-specific trial-only statute. Government-building symbols Q11 is an impartiality-principle inference, not a claimed nationwide art ban. Flag File page, named authorship and PD-shape status verified; local 960×600 PNG visually inspected. No target scores or neighbouring answers used. Independent parent audit, archive, shared credits and browser integration remain pending. Validation results recorded after running the repository validator. Initial validation found one duplicate Freedom House URL and a year-only date; these were corrected. The final validator blocks archive on the four explicitly null answers and warns about supported mixed/conditional answers in assimilation, ownership, trade and causation. These warnings were individually reviewed; no unknown was converted to Neutral. No similarity neighbours are returned for the incomplete draft. Focused continuation on 2026-10-05 by primary OpenAI Codex agent /root: Read the current psychology syllabus (effective 1 February 2026) and reread 1177 guidance for ages 6–7. Teaching biological emotions, social factors and comparison of models does not adopt the precise causal rankings for national IQ, general interests or immediate moral intuitions. Checked the Defence University perspective of 8 March 2022, the 2010 inquiry manual and FIB 2019:1. Academic discussion and an inquiry proposal do not establish adoption of an anticipatory-force rule; FIB sets training requirements without adopting that rule. The indexed IKFN 2016 PDF failed retrieval (404), so its text/current status was not verified. Tactical or personal self-defence cannot automatically settle state anticipatory self-defence. All 4 exact question-level gaps remain null/unknown. Existing supported answers, period and cutoff are preserved. This was a focused same-agent research and separate challenge pass, not a complete independent re-review or publication sign-off. Separate completion pass on 2026-10-05: checked the 4 new educated assumptions against exact question wording, agreement direction, contextual sources and prior withdrawal reasons. These are most-likely provisional estimates, not adopted national causal theories. The distinction between individual and national/racial heredity, immediate intuition and deliberate instruction, and interventions and causal predominance is retained. Assumption IDs: culture-nature-02, culture-nature-05, culture-nature-10, militarist-pacifist-04. Reviewed neutral-heavy axis rationales: explicit mixed institutions, competing implemented rules and interaction models justify retained neutral choices; uncertainty alone was not used as the neutral rationale. Earlier whole-assessment review is preserved; this continuation does not claim a fresh independent 240-source reread or a human review. Similarity and browser checks are recorded separately after integration.

neutralAnswers.rationale: Educated assumption: Institutional inference: Ordinary national referendums are advisory; a defined binding vote can reject a pending constitutional amendment. This is a limited mixed framework rather than a general repeal power. Most likely Neutral. The cited facts provide contextual evidence for an institutional estimate, not a verified explicit national endorsement of this exact statement. Formal constitutional provisions do not alone establish their practical independence or an explicit endorsement of the exact institutional rule.
